title: India's Industrial Waste & Recycling Economy
subtitle: Battery metals, e-waste, chemical recovery and the secondary-industrial opportunity across Indian recycling corridors
summary: A strategic read across India's emergent recycling economy — battery metals, e-waste streams, black mass, chemical recovery and the investment logic of secondary industrial corridors.

signal.excerpt: India's recycling economy is shifting from waste management to industrial infrastructure — battery metals, e-waste and chemical recovery are becoming strategic corridors.
takeaways: Battery metals and black mass recovery are emerging as high-value secondary-industrial nodes in India's recycling economy.
E-waste streams now carry recoverable aluminium, copper, lithium and critical-mineral fractions that domestic capacity does not fully capture.
Chemical recovery and refining are the binding constraints — not collection — and define where investment actually accrues.
